text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Trade Minister Le Van Triet said that only by enhancing the competitiveness of its economy can Vietnam catch up with other countries.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has called for the establishment of a special police force to safeguard the forests in the central highlands.
-- Vietnam plans to equitize the telecom equipment and cable plant Sacom, which is based in the southern province of Dong Nai. The company expects to issue 2,400 shares worth $109,200.

-- Negotiations between Vietnam and foreign companies on a contract to sell gas extracted from the South Con Son Basin have not been finalised. Gas reserves in the area have been estimated at 58 billion cubic metres.
-- The United Nations will pay compensation to Vietnamese workers who had their labour contracts with Iraq and Kuwait's authorities terminated by the Gulf War in early 1990.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has approved a plan to increase electricity prices throughout the country by at least ten percent from May 15.
-- More than 200 corruption cases causing losses of $15.5 million were uncovered by the State Inspector over the last six months.
